title: Acute cellular renal allograft rejection: cell-mediated immunity
vignette: A 62-year-old woman with long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus experiences progressive renal decline over 4-5 years despite optimal blood pressure control. She is given interim hemodialysis and eventually undergoes transplantation of a deceased donor renal allograft. Three weeks after surgery, she experiences generalized malaise. Medical history is significant for diabetic retinopathy and osteoporosis, and her current medications include tacrolimus, mycophenolate sodium, and low-dose prednisone. Laboratory results: potassium 5.2 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 45 mg/dL, creatinine 3.1 mg/dL, glucose 123 mg/dL, and calcium 10.0 mg/dL. The patient undergoes percutaneous biopsy of the transplanted kidney, and light microscopy of the obtained tissue reveals a dense mononuclear infiltrate involving the blood vessels, tubules, and interstitium. Which of the following processes is most likely responsible for this patient's current condition?

clues.note: Onset within the first weeks-to-months after transplant is the classic timing of ACUTE rejection.
A rising serum creatinine (3.1) signals allograft dysfunction - here from acute rejection injuring the transplanted kidney.

clues.text: dense mononuclear infiltrate involving the blood vessels, tubules, and interstitium
clues.note: A lymphocytic (mononuclear) infiltrate of graft vessels (endotheliitis), tubules, and interstitium is the histologic hallmark of acute CELLULAR (T-cell-mediated) rejection.

whatMatters: Rising creatinine a few weeks after a kidney transplant, with biopsy showing a dense LYMPHOCYTIC (mononuclear) infiltrate of vessels, tubules, and interstitium = ACUTE CELLULAR rejection. It is mediated by recipient T cells sensitized to donor antigens - CELL-MEDIATED IMMUNITY. Answer A.
strategy: Anchor on timing (weeks-months) + biopsy (lymphocytic interstitial/tubular infiltrate with endotheliitis) = acute cellular rejection (T-cell/cell-mediated). Reject calcineurin-inhibitor (tacrolimus) toxicity (arteriolar hyalinosis/tubular vacuolization, not a dense lymphocytic infiltrate), immune-complex vasculitis (glomerular, e.g., lupus/HSP), renovascular disease (ischemic fibrosis/atrophy), and volume depletion (acute tubular necrosis, no lymphocytic infiltrate).

eliminations.label: Drug toxicity - calcineurin inhibitor changes differ
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: calcineurin-inhibitor (tacrolimus/cyclosporine) nephrotoxicity. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it shows arteriolar hyalinosis and isometric tubular vacuolization, NOT a dense mononuclear infiltrate of vessels/tubules/interstitium. ✅ Correct if: biopsy shows tubular vacuolization/arteriolar hyalinosis without lymphocytic infiltrate.

eliminations.label: Immune complex vasculitis - glomerular, not interstitial
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: immune-complex deposition (e.g., lupus, Henoch-Schonlein) causing proliferative glomerulonephritis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it produces glomerular hypercellularity/immune deposits, not the tubulointerstitial lymphocytic infiltrate of cellular rejection. ✅ Correct if: glomerulonephritis with immune-complex deposits.

eliminations.label: Renovascular disease - ischemic, chronic changes (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: chronic renovascular disease (e.g., renal artery stenosis) causing ischemia. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it produces diffuse ischemic changes - interstitial fibrosis, glomerular crowding, tubular atrophy - not an acute dense lymphocytic infiltrate. ✅ Correct if: chronic ischemic atrophy/fibrosis from vascular narrowing.

eliminations.label: Volume depletion - acute tubular necrosis, no infiltrate
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: prerenal/ischemic injury from hypovolemia causing acute tubular necrosis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: ATN shows tubular epithelial necrosis WITHOUT a lymphocytic infiltrate; this biopsy shows dense mononuclear inflammation. ✅ Correct if: tubular necrosis with muddy-brown casts after hypotension.

reasoning: Rising creatinine ~3 weeks post-transplant = acute allograft rejection
Biopsy: dense lymphocytic (mononuclear) infiltrate of vessels (endotheliitis), tubules, interstitium
This is acute CELLULAR rejection, mediated by recipient T cells against donor antigens
mechanism: Acute rejection typically occurs within the first 6 months after transplantation and can be cell-mediated or antibody-mediated. In ACUTE CELLULAR rejection, recipient T lymphocytes become sensitized to donor (allogeneic) MHC antigens and mount a CELL-MEDIATED response: cytotoxic and helper T cells infiltrate the graft, producing a dense lymphocytic (mononuclear) interstitial infiltrate with tubulitis and inflammation of the vascular endothelium (endotheliitis) - exactly the biopsy picture here, with rising creatinine and malaise. Immunosuppressants such as tacrolimus (a calcineurin inhibitor) and mycophenolate are used to prevent this T-cell response, and episodes are treated with increased immunosuppression (e.g., steroids). The distractors have different histology: calcineurin-inhibitor toxicity (arteriolar hyalinosis/tubular vacuolization), immune-complex glomerulonephritis (glomerular deposits), chronic renovascular disease (ischemic fibrosis/atrophy), and volume depletion (acute tubular necrosis) - none shows a dense tubulointerstitial lymphocytic infiltrate.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Immuno > transplant rejection: hyperacute (preformed antibodies, minutes), acute cellular (T-cell, weeks-months, lymphocytic interstitial infiltrate + endotheliitis), acute humoral (C4d), chronic (fibrosis).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Timing (weeks) + lymphocytic tubulointerstitial infiltrate = acute cellular (T-cell/cell-mediated) rejection.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on cell-mediated vs humoral rejection, endotheliitis, tubulitis, calcineurin-inhibitor toxicity, or allograft? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Calcineurin toxicity (tubular vacuolization), immune-complex GN (glomerular), renovascular (ischemic fibrosis), volume depletion (ATN) lack the dense lymphocytic infiltrate.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: acute cellular rejection = T-cell-mediated, lymphocytic interstitial/tubular infiltrate + endotheliitis; treat with increased immunosuppression.

keywords.front: Rising creatinine weeks post-transplant + lymphocytic interstitial infiltrate
Immune mechanism of acute cellular rejection
keywords.back: Cell-mediated immunity (recipient T cells vs donor antigens)
Preformed recipient antibodies; minutes to hours
Vascular wall thickening, interstitial fibrosis, tubular atrophy (months-years)

firstAid.detail: Immuno: T-cell-mediated, weeks-months; lymphocytic interstitial infiltrate + endotheliitis.

memoryHook: Weeks after a new kidney, recipient T cells swarm the graft's tubules and vessels - a lymphocytic ambush = acute cellular (cell-mediated) rejection.
